Question: What does it mean that Jesus redeemed us?
ShortAnswer: To say Jesus redeemed us means He paid the price to set us free from sin and death. Like a slave bought out of bondage, we now belong to Him — not as property to be used, but as beloved people brought home.
DetailedAnswer: In the ancient world, redemption was a marketplace word: paying a ransom to free a slave or a prisoner of war. Jesus used it for Himself: 'the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many' (Mark 10:45). Paul echoes it: Christ 'gave himself as a ransom for all people' (1 Timothy 2:6), and Titus says He 'gave himself for us to redeem us from all wickedness and to purify for himself a people that are his very own' (Titus 2:14). The price was His own life, poured out on the cross; the freedom is comprehensive — from sin's guilt, its power, and one day its presence. And redemption changes ownership in the best way: 'You are not your own; you were bought at a price' (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). That is not grim servitude; it is belonging. A redeemed person is someone who was headed for judgment and is now headed home, someone who was a slave and is now a son or daughter, someone whose life is no longer defined by what enslaved them but by the One who paid to set them free.
